% ================================================================
% Reading scales and error intervals.
%
% A Year 7 sheet on how accurate a measurement read from a scale is.
% Part 1 shows enlarged views of the scales on rulers, a metre rule,
% a measuring jug, a measuring cylinder, kitchen scales, luggage
% scales and a river depth gauge. Pupils work out what one gap
% between two ticks is worth, then round each measurement to the
% nearest tick. The scaffold under each picture fades as the part
% goes on.
%
% Part 2 introduces the lower bound, the upper bound and the error
% interval of a reading. The worked example is a metre rule marked
% in centimetres, which is accurate to plus or minus 0.5 cm. It is
% followed by the same layout with gaps, then the same layout with
% fewer gaps, then the readings from Part 1 again with only the
% inequality as a frame, and then a table of measurements with no
% frame. Part 3 has reverse problems, questions about whether a
% reading can be trusted, a scale for pupils to design, and ends
% with an open task about an instrument of their own choosing.
%
% The sheet is written on and is four sides of A4. The \newpage
% commands are placed so that no question is split across a page.
%
% In every picture the end of the object, the surface of the liquid
% or the pointer is drawn 0.3 or 0.7 of a gap past a tick, so that
% the nearest tick is clear and a reading is never a halfway case.
% Each picture is drawn from the value in the comment beside it, so
% a reading can be changed by changing one coordinate.
%
% Readings: Q1 14 cm, Q2 76 cm, Q3 340 ml, Q4 36 ml, Q5 440 g,
% Q6 5.4 cm, Q7 23.6 kg, Q8 1.3 m.
% ================================================================

% ----------------------------------------------------------------
% Close-up pictures of scales.
%
% Each picture is clipped to a rounded window between \zoomclip and
% \zoomframe, and a small magnifying glass on the corner of the
% window shows that the view is enlarged.
\tikzset{
  tick/.style={line width=0.5pt},
  ticklab/.style={font=\scriptsize, inner sep=1.5pt},
  scalebody/.style={fill=yellow!7, draw=black!60, line width=0.5pt},
  water/.style={fill=blue!13},
  surface/.style={blue!60!black, line width=0.9pt},
}
\newcommand{\zoomclip}[4]{%
  \def\zxa{#1}\def\zya{#2}\def\zxb{#3}\def\zyb{#4}%
  \begin{scope}\clip[rounded corners=6pt] (#1,#2) rectangle (#3,#4);}
\newcommand{\zoomframe}{%
  \end{scope}
  \draw[black!55, line width=0.9pt, rounded corners=6pt] (\zxa,\zya) rectangle (\zxb,\zyb);
  \draw[black!55, line width=1.8pt, line cap=round] ($(\zxb,\zyb)+(0.14,0.14)$) -- ++(0.22,0.22);
  \draw[black!55, line width=0.8pt, fill=white] (\zxb,\zyb) circle (0.19);}

% Ticks along the top edge of a horizontal scale, hanging down from
% y = 0, with tick i at x = i times the gap.
% \hticks{first i}{last i}{cm per gap}{label every}{longer tick every}{value at i=0}{value per gap}
\newcommand{\hticks}[7]{%
  \foreach \i in {#1,...,#2}{%
    \pgfmathtruncatemacro{\islab}{ifthenelse(mod(\i,#4)==0,1,0)}%
    \pgfmathtruncatemacro{\ismid}{ifthenelse(mod(\i,#5)==0,1,0)}%
    \ifnum\islab=1
      \draw[tick] ({\i*(#3)},0) -- ++(0,-0.5);
      \pgfmathsetmacro{\val}{#6+\i*(#7)}%
      \node[ticklab,below] at ({\i*(#3)},-0.5) {\pgfmathprintnumber{\val}};
    \else\ifnum\ismid=1
      \draw[tick] ({\i*(#3)},0) -- ++(0,-0.36);
    \else
      \draw[tick] ({\i*(#3)},0) -- ++(0,-0.22);
    \fi\fi}}

% Ticks up the side of a vertical scale, pointing right from x = 0,
% with tick i at y = i times the gap. A negative gap makes the values
% increase downwards.
% \vticks{first i}{last i}{cm per gap}{label every}{longer tick every}{value at i=0}{value per gap}{unit}
\newcommand{\vticks}[8]{%
  \foreach \i in {#1,...,#2}{%
    \pgfmathtruncatemacro{\islab}{ifthenelse(mod(\i,#4)==0,1,0)}%
    \pgfmathtruncatemacro{\ismid}{ifthenelse(mod(\i,#5)==0,1,0)}%
    \ifnum\islab=1
      \draw[tick] (0,{\i*(#3)}) -- ++(0.75,0);
      \pgfmathsetmacro{\val}{#6+\i*(#7)}%
      \node[ticklab,right] at (0.75,{\i*(#3)}) {\pgfmathprintnumber{\val}\,#8};
    \else\ifnum\ismid=1
      \draw[tick] (0,{\i*(#3)}) -- ++(0.55,0);
    \else
      \draw[tick] (0,{\i*(#3)}) -- ++(0.38,0);
    \fi\fi}}

% A pencil lying along the top of a ruler, with its tip at x = #1.
\newcommand{\pencil}[1]{%
  \filldraw[fill=yellow!35, draw=black!70] (-3,0.05) rectangle ({#1-1.0},0.59);
  \draw[black!35] (-3,0.32) -- ({#1-1.0},0.32);
  \filldraw[fill=orange!15, draw=black!70] ({#1-1.0},0.05) -- (#1,0.32) -- ({#1-1.0},0.59) -- cycle;
  \fill[black!65] ({#1-0.3},0.239) -- (#1,0.32) -- ({#1-0.3},0.401) -- cycle;}

% Part 1 layouts. A horizontal picture goes between the question and
% its answer lines. A tall picture goes to the left, with the
% question and answer lines beside it.
\newcommand{\hcell}[3]{%
  \begin{minipage}[t]{0.485\linewidth}
  #1\par\smallskip
  {\centering #2\par}\smallskip
  #3
  \end{minipage}}
\newcommand{\vcell}[3]{%
  \begin{minipage}[t]{0.485\linewidth}
  \begin{minipage}[t]{3.95cm}\vspace{0pt}#2\end{minipage}\hfill
  \begin{minipage}[t]{\dimexpr\linewidth-4.15cm\relax}\vspace{0pt}\raggedright #1\par\medskip #3\end{minipage}
  \end{minipage}}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------
% A number line for an error interval: three ticks one gap apart,
% then any extra drawing (the interval itself in the worked example).
\newcommand{\numline}[4]{%
  \begin{tikzpicture}[x=2.3cm, baseline=(current bounding box.north)]
  \draw[line width=0.7pt, {Stealth[length=5pt]}-{Stealth[length=5pt]}] (-0.4,0) -- (2.4,0);
  \foreach \x/\l in {0/#1,1/#2,2/#3}{%
    \draw[tick] (\x,0.15) -- (\x,-0.15);
    \node[ticklab,below] at (\x,-0.17) {\l};}
  #4
  \end{tikzpicture}}

\newpage
\parttitle{2}{\ealgloss{Error intervals}{przedziały błędu}}

\begin{keyidea}
\begin{ealglossed}
When we read a \ealgloss{scale}{skalować} to the nearest \ealgloss{tick}{kreski}, the \ealgloss{reading}{odczyt} is not the \ealgloss{exact}{ścisłym}
\ealgloss{measurement}{pomiarem}. The true \ealgloss{measurement}{pomiar} could be up to half of one \ealgloss{gap}{odstępu} below the
\ealgloss{reading}{odczytu}, or up to half of one \ealgloss{gap}{odstępu} above it. On a metre rule marked in
centimetres one \ealgloss{gap}{odstęp} is 1\,cm, so a \ealgloss{reading}{odczyt} of 73\,cm is \ealgloss{accurate}{dokładny} to
$\pm\,0.5$\,cm. The symbol $\pm$ means ``\ealgloss{plus or minus}{plus minus}''.
\end{ealglossed}

\smallskip
\begin{ealglossed}
The smallest value the true \ealgloss{measurement}{pomiar} could be is the \textbf{\ealgloss{lower bound}{dolna granica}}.
The true \ealgloss{measurement}{pomiar} must be less than the \textbf{\ealgloss{upper bound}{ograniczenie górne}}: a \ealgloss{length}{długość} of
exactly 73.5\,cm is halfway between two \ealgloss{ticks}{kreskami}, and halfway values are \ealgloss{rounded up}{zaokrąglane w górę}, so it would be read as 74\,cm.
\end{ealglossed}

\smallskip
\begin{ealglossed}
The \textbf{\ealgloss{error interval}{przedział błędu}} gives every value the true \ealgloss{measurement}{pomiar} could be.
We write it with the \ealgloss{inequality}{nierówności} symbols $\le$, which means ``is less than or
equal to'', and $<$, which means ``is less than''.
\end{ealglossed}
\end{keyidea}

\begin{wex}{a metre rule marked in centimetres}
\begin{ealglossed}
A table is measured with a metre rule marked in centimetres. The \ealgloss{reading}{odczyt} to the
nearest \ealgloss{tick}{kreski} is 73\,cm.
\end{ealglossed}

\smallskip
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.61\linewidth}\vspace{0pt}
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{2.0}
\begin{tabular}{@{}ll@{}}

\ealgloss{Gap}{odstęp} between two \ealgloss{ticks}{kreskami} & 1\,cm\\
Half of the \ealgloss{gap}{odstępu} & $1\div2=0.5$\,cm\\
\ealgloss{Lower bound}{dolna granica} & $73-0.5=72.5$\,cm\\
\ealgloss{Upper bound}{ograniczenie górne} & $73+0.5=73.5$\,cm\\
\ealgloss{Error interval}{przedział błędu} & $72.5\,\text{cm}\le\text{length}<73.5\,\text{cm}$
\end{tabular}
\end{minipage}\hfill

\begin{enumerate}[resume]

\end{ealglossed}

\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{2.2}

(b) $245\,\text{g}\le\text{mass}<255\,\text{g}$ & \ealgloss{Reading}{odczyt}: \ansline[1.8cm] & \ealgloss{Gap}{odstęp}: \ansline[1.8cm]\\
(c) $1.35\,\text{m}\le\text{height}<1.45\,\text{m}$ & \ealgloss{Reading}{odczyt}: \ansline[1.8cm] & \ealgloss{Gap}{odstęp}: \ansline[1.8cm]

\item \begin{ealglossed}
Leo weighs his suitcase with luggage \ealgloss{scales}{skalować} marked every 0.2\,kg. The
\ealgloss{reading}{odczyt} is 23.0\,kg. His airline allows suitcases with a \ealgloss{mass}{masą} of 23\,kg or
less. Can Leo be sure that his suitcase is allowed? Explain using the \ealgloss{error interval}{przedział błędu}.
\end{ealglossed}
\wline\wline\wline

\item \begin{ealglossed}
Sam measures a leaf with a ruler marked in millimetres. Sam says, ``The
\ealgloss{ticks}{kreski} on my ruler are very close together, so the leaf is exactly 6.3\,cm
long.'' Is Sam right? Explain.
\end{ealglossed}
\wline\wline\wline

\newpage
\item \begin{ealglossed}
A biscuit recipe works if the \ealgloss{mass}{masa} of butter is \ealgloss{at least}{co najmniej} 195\,g and less
than 205\,g. A chef adds butter to a bowl until the \ealgloss{scales}{skalować} read 200\,g. \ealgloss{Scales}{skalować}
A are marked every 10\,g. \ealgloss{Scales}{skalować} B are marked every 50\,g.
\end{ealglossed}
\begin{enumerate}
\item \begin{ealglossed}
Write the \ealgloss{error interval}{przedział błędu} for the \ealgloss{reading}{odczyt} of 200\,g on \ealgloss{scales}{skalować} A.\\[4pt]
\ansline[1.6cm]\,g $\le$ \ealgloss{mass}{masa} $<$ \ansline[1.6cm]\,g
\end{ealglossed}
\item \begin{ealglossed}
Write the \ealgloss{error interval}{przedział błędu} for the \ealgloss{reading}{odczyt} of 200\,g on \ealgloss{scales}{skalować} B.\\[4pt]
\ansline[1.6cm]\,g $\le$ \ealgloss{mass}{masa} $<$ \ansline[1.6cm]\,g
\end{ealglossed}
\item \begin{ealglossed}
Which \ealgloss{scales}{skalować} should the chef use? Explain.
\end{ealglossed}
\wline\wline
\end{enumerate}

\item \begin{ealglossed}
\textbf{Challenge.} Ana measures a shelf with a metre rule marked in
centimetres, and the \ealgloss{reading}{odczyt} is 80\,cm. She measures the \ealgloss{gap}{odstęp} between two walls
with the same metre rule, and the \ealgloss{reading}{odczyt} is also 80\,cm. Will the shelf
definitely fit in the \ealgloss{gap}{odstępie}? Explain using \ealgloss{error intervals}{przedziałów błędu}.
\end{ealglossed}
\wline\wline\wline\wline

\item \begin{ealglossed}
Choose a measuring instrument at home or at school, such as bathroom
\ealgloss{scales}{skalować}, a measuring spoon or a tape measure.
\end{ealglossed}
\begin{enumerate}
\item \begin{ealglossed}
Name the instrument, and say how far apart the \ealgloss{ticks}{kreski} on its \ealgloss{scale}{skalować} are.
\end{ealglossed}
\wline
\item \begin{ealglossed}
Make up a \ealgloss{reading}{odczyt} on this \ealgloss{scale}{skalować}, and write its \ealgloss{error interval}{przedział błędu}.
\end{ealglossed}
\wline
\item \begin{ealglossed}
Describe one job that this instrument is \ealgloss{accurate}{dokładny} enough for, and one
job that it is not \ealgloss{accurate}{dokładny} enough for. Explain using the \ealgloss{error interval}{przedział błędu}.
\end{ealglossed}
\wline\wline\wline
\end{enumerate}
